news: DGTR concluded its anti-dumping probe and recommended definitive duties on borosilicate table and kitchen glassware from China, on Borosil's application. Stock rose ~6% intraday on 28-Sep before paring to ~4.6%. Analysts estimate ~Rs 22 cr FY28 EBITDA uplift (if 50% of the price benefit is captured) and raised FY28 PAT by ~9%. The Finance Ministry notification is still pending.
market_consensus_gap: The Street still values Borosil's consumer glassware as a low-growth franchise facing a flood of cheap Chinese imports that caps realisations. Once the duty is notified (typically within ~3 months), import landed costs are reset for 5 years. That restores pricing power and utilisation at its Jaipur and Bharuch borosilicate capacity. Only a partial, single-house EPS change is in the price so far.
reflexivity_thesis: 1) Finance Ministry notification converts the recommendation into a hard floor on import prices. 2) Channel restocking shifts to domestic supply, so Borosil takes price increases and gains share in e-commerce and modern trade. 3) Operating leverage on underutilised capacity means sell-side raises EPS across the board (FY27E-28E), not only the first 9% revision. 4) A small/mid-cap consumer name with a visible margin story attracts DII consumer and midcap funds. 5) A higher multiple on higher EPS feeds the loop. Watch: the notification in the Gazette and the duty quantum per tonne.

catalyst_category: L1 Tender Status (pre-LoA) + Private Capex LoIs
news: Newly listed (17-Sep-2026) LCC Projects emerged L1 for a Rs 653.34 cr Govt of Rajasthan EPC contract (Chhoti Kalisindh irrigation project), which is not yet awarded. On 28-Sep it also received two LoIs worth Rs 70.35 cr from Reliance Industries for civil works on a 400 kV substation in Kutch, Gujarat. Its pre-IPO order book was Rs 7,953 cr (Mar-2026).
market_consensus_gap: As a fresh IPO with thin analyst coverage, the market prices LCC on its pre-IPO order book alone. The L1 bid and a first Reliance relationship show post-IPO order inflow running ahead of plan, and they open a private-capex (RIL transmission) pipeline beyond state irrigation.
reflexivity_thesis: 1) The Rs 653 cr L1 converts to an LoA, taking post-listing inflows past Rs 720 cr within 2 weeks. 2) Order book/revenue coverage rises, and the first initiating-coverage reports model higher FY27-28 revenue. 3) An RIL repeat-order optionality narrative draws small-cap funds once the anchor lock-in dynamics settle. 4) Rising market cap improves its bidding capacity (net-worth-linked), which brings more wins. Risk: anchor lock-in expiry, and state payment cycles.

news: NCLAT set aside the NCLT Amaravati dismissal of the GOCL-Hinduja National Power (HNPCL) merger first motion and directed the NCLT to appoint a chairman and scrutinisers and hold shareholder and creditor meetings by 5-Oct-2026. Swap ratio: 206 GOCL shares per 10,000 HNPCL shares. HNPCL has 1,040 MW operating thermal capacity plus 600 MW of planned expansion.
market_consensus_gap: After the July NCLT rejection, the market wrote off or heavily discounted the merger and treats GOCL as an explosives/realty holdco. The NCLAT order puts the scheme back on a firm procedural timeline. GOCL would absorb a cash-generating 1 GW regulated power utility, which is a category change for the stock.
reflexivity_thesis: 1) Shareholder and creditor meetings by 5-Oct approve the scheme, which removes the legal-risk discount. 2) Second-motion filing and sanction follow, and the Street starts SOTP modelling with HNPCL's regulated RoE cash flows. 3) The power-utility re-rating attracts utilities/thermal-theme funds. 4) The Hinduja group's commitment signal (600 MW expansion) sustains the narrative. Risk: dilution from the swap, and a fresh NCLT objection.

news: Ellenbarrie won a Rs 480.73 cr BHEL contract to supply and erect a 1,200 TPD cryogenic Air Separation Unit for the 2,000 TPD coal-to-ammonium-nitrate project at Bandhabal, Odisha. Commissioning is targeted for FY29. The order exceeds the company's entire FY25 revenue (Rs 348 cr).
market_consensus_gap: Consensus models Ellenbarrie as a merchant/on-site industrial gas seller. This is its first large engineering (ASU EPC) win, a high-barrier segment dominated by global majors. It also ties into India's coal-gasification mission, where many ASUs will be needed.
reflexivity_thesis: 1) The order exceeds a year of revenue, so FY27-29 revenue estimates must be rebuilt with a new EPC segment. 2) Validation from a BHEL reference makes Ellenbarrie a credible bidder for the coal-gasification ASU pipeline (Coal India/BHEL JV, NLC, private). 3) A new-segment TAM story brings re-rating toward capital-goods multiples. 4) Recently IPO'd with a small float, so DII inclusion drives price, and the loop continues. Risk: EPC margin dilution and execution to FY29.

news: The board approved a ~Rs 526 cr preferential issue to institutional and non-promoter investors (RK Damani entity and Asha Mukul Agrawal among them) for expansion and acquisitions (semiconductor/ESDM engineering). EGM on 4-Oct-2026.
market_consensus_gap: The stock ran to a record high on the names involved, but the Street has not modelled what Rs 526 cr of growth capital does for a small ER&D/semicap-equipment company: inorganic acquisitions and a scale-up of India OSAT/semiconductor tooling. The funding is well above its current capital base.
reflexivity_thesis: 1) EGM approval on 4-Oct locks in capital from marquee long-term holders, which lowers perceived risk. 2) Deployment into acquisitions and capacity makes growth visible in the semiconductor supply chain (ISM-linked). 3) Sell-side and PMS coverage starts, which widens the holder base. 4) India semicon theme flows bring reflexive momentum. Risk: dilution, and a rich valuation after the rally.

news: Dilip Buildcon was declared L-1 bidder for a Rs 688.23 cr (ex-GST) NHAI HAM project: a 4-lane 9.66 km elevated corridor on NH-65 at Solapur (Old Pune Naka to Boramani Naka), with 24-month construction and a 15-year O&M/annuity period. LoA is pending.
market_consensus_gap: The market treats DBL as a road contractor that is ex-growth amid NHAI award drought. A steady flow of HAM L1s signals NHAI tendering is revived into H2 FY27. Elevated corridors also carry better margins than plain at-grade roads.
reflexivity_thesis: 1) L1 converts to LoA, and order inflow tracks above guidance. 2) HAM annuity assets can be monetised via the InvIT (Shrem/DBL platforms), so equity is recycled. 3) Order-inflow beats lead sell-side to upgrade FY28 revenue. 4) An 'NHAI award cycle turning' narrative lifts the infra EPC basket. Risk: aggressive L1 pricing and working capital.

news: Chemplast Sanmar partially resumed operations at its Karaikal EDC (ethylene dichloride) plant after the Puducherry Pollution Control Committee provisionally revoked the prohibition order. The plant had been shut since the July-2026 fire and closure directive. Final revocation is pending.
market_consensus_gap: The market has priced a prolonged shutdown, with EDC bought in from outside and hurting the specialty-PVC/caustic chain margins. A restart restores backward integration. Combined with the PVC anti-dumping regime, this sets up a margin recovery the Street has not yet modelled.
reflexivity_thesis: 1) Final PPCC revocation leads to full ramp-up and removes purchased-EDC costs. 2) H2 FY27 EBITDA recovers sharply off a depressed base, and consensus upgrades follow. 3) Short covering plus return of chemical-cyclical funds. 4) A PVC price upcycle (import duties) compounds the effect. Risk: conditions attached to the restart, and PVC price volatility.

catalyst_category: Regulatory Dialogue / New Market Licence (Coal Exchange)
news: IEX's wholly-owned subsidiary Indian Coal Exchange Ltd applied on 25-Sep-2026 to the Coal Controller's Organisation for registration and a licence to operate a coal exchange.
market_consensus_gap: Consensus is anchored on the market-coupling threat to IEX's power-exchange monopoly and its de-rating. A coal exchange is a new TAM (India trades ~1 bn t of coal) that is not in any estimate and would diversify away from the coupling risk.
reflexivity_thesis: 1) Grant of the licence gives first-mover status in the coal trading platform. 2) Volume-based fees on coal e-auctions and commercial mining output create a new EPS line. 3) The narrative shifts from 'coupling loser' to 'multi-commodity energy exchange', so the multiple de-rating reverses. 4) FIIs that exited on coupling fears return. Risk: licence competition (MCX/NSE/PXIL), and a CERC coupling order.

news: The Madhya Pradesh High Court directed the state to renew Som Distilleries' manufacturing licences within 15 days and awarded Rs 1 lakh in costs against the state government. The stock jumped ~10.6%.
market_consensus_gap: The licence suspension had capped Som's MP home-market volumes and created an existential governance discount. A court-mandated renewal with costs against the state removes the overhang. The volume recovery in beer (strong-beer leadership) is not yet in estimates.
reflexivity_thesis: 1) Renewal within 15 days restores MP production ahead of the peak season. 2) Volume normalisation plus operating leverage leads to sharp EPS revisions. 3) The governance/regulatory discount narrows, and small-cap funds return. Risk: state appeal, and governance history.

news: NMDC commissioned its 2 MTPA pellet plant at Nagarnar, Chhattisgarh, part of a Rs 5,427 cr integrated project with a 135-km slurry pipeline from Bailadila, beneficiation and pelletisation.
market_consensus_gap: NMDC is priced as a pure iron-ore-price proxy. Moving into pellets plus slurry-pipeline logistics structurally lowers freight cost and captures the value-add margin. Sell-side has not yet modelled this new integrated earnings stream.
reflexivity_thesis: 1) Pellet volume ramp brings higher realisation per tonne and lower rail freight. 2) EBITDA/t upgrades follow, and the PSU re-rates on 'value-added miner'. 3) The dividend yield plus a growth angle draws DII PSU funds. Risk: iron ore prices, and ramp-up delays.

catalyst_category: Hidden CapEx / Fleet Expansion + Rights Issue
news: Dredging Corporation of India plans 11 new dredgers over 5 years (Rs 3,560 cr capex) through Indian shipyard partnerships, and is considering a ~Rs 1,000 cr rights issue. It turned profitable in FY26 (revenue Rs 1,208 cr).
market_consensus_gap: Consensus sees DCI as a loss-prone, ageing-fleet PSU. The Maritime India Vision push (port deepening, Sagarmala) plus fleet doubling changes its capacity ceiling, and a rights issue from major-port shareholders signals sovereign backing.
reflexivity_thesis: 1) Rights issue with the anchor ports subscribing gives a funding certainty signal. 2) Fleet additions lift revenue capacity 2x over 5 years. 3) The shipbuilding/maritime theme basket pulls in momentum flows. Risk: rights dilution, and execution by Indian yards.

news: Morepen filed its first-ever US ANDA, for Sitagliptin tablets (25/50/100 mg), leveraging its API integration and positioning in CDMO.
market_consensus_gap: Morepen is valued as a domestic API/OTC/diagnostics business. A first US ANDA marks entry into regulated formulations and a validated CDMO capability, a narrative inflection even though revenue is 12-24 months out.
reflexivity_thesis: 1) ANDA acceptance and a USFDA facility inspection unlock US formulations. 2) Vertical integration in the gliptin API gives a cost edge post-Januvia generics. 3) The pipeline of further ANDAs brings re-rating toward formulation peers. Risk: a crowded sitagliptin market, and inspection outcome.

news: Promoter group entity Nirayu Pvt Ltd bought 1.67 lakh Alembic Ltd shares in the open market, continuing its creeping acquisition.
market_consensus_gap: Alembic Ltd trades at a steep holdco discount to its stake in Alembic Pharma plus its real estate. Persistent promoter buying signals that insiders see value, and it hints at eventual holdco simplification.
reflexivity_thesis: 1) Creeping acquisition reduces the free float. 2) A holdco-discount narrowing narrative. 3) Realty monetisation (Vadodara land) is a potential trigger. Risk: small size of purchases.

news: Vikram Solar secured a 400 MW N-type TOPCon module supply order from an EPC customer for agri-solar (PM-KUSUM/MSKVY) projects in Maharashtra.
market_consensus_gap: The Street worries about module oversupply and price erosion after the IPO. Steady DCR/TOPCon orders from distributed agri-solar show demand pockets where ALMM/DCR protection holds pricing.
reflexivity_thesis: 1) The order book supports utilisation of its new TOPCon lines. 2) ALMM List-II (cells) from Jun-2026 favours integrated players. 3) Estimate stability draws funds back to the sector. Risk: module price deflation and a crowded sector.

news: Welspun Corp's US subsidiary won its largest-ever HFIW pipe order (USD 412.5 mn, ~Rs 3,600-4,000 cr). The global order book is at a record USD 4.7 bn. The stock rose ~4%.
market_consensus_gap: The order itself is partly priced in, but consensus undervalues the multi-year US energy pipeline cycle and the Little Rock HFIW/HSAW capacity utilisation under US tariff protection.
reflexivity_thesis: 1) A record order book gives 2+ years of visibility. 2) US tariffs on imported pipe protect the US plant margins. 3) EPS upgrades follow, then FII buying. Risk: partly priced in (Stage-2 leaning).

company_name: Power Grid Corporation of India Limited
news: Power Grid won a Maharashtra ISTS TBCB project (Rs 430.67 cr annual charges), its 9th TBCB win this FY. The board approved a Rs 10,000 cr unsecured term loan from SBI.
market_consensus_gap: The market sees POWERGRID as a slow-growth bond proxy. The TBCB win rate and debt-funded capex signal accelerating regulated-asset growth (capex guidance could be raised).
reflexivity_thesis: 1) Wins lead to capex upgrades and faster RAB growth. 2) EPS CAGR re-rated from ~5% to ~10%. 3) DII defensive-growth allocation follows. Risk: large-cap, slow mover.

news: Promoter group entity Nirani Holdings bought ~1.52 lakh shares in the open market, continuing repeated small purchases. Earlier, the promoter pledged 14 lakh shares to Jio Credit.
market_consensus_gap: The market discounts TruAlt on ethanol-cycle and pledge concerns. Consistent promoter buying suggests insiders see value ahead of ethanol blending (E27/E30) and CBG/SAF plans.
reflexivity_thesis: 1) Accumulation reduces float. 2) Policy on E27/SAF blending targets. 3) The ethanol theme rerates. Risk: the pledge offsets the signal.

news: INOX India supplied 2,200-litre LNG fuel systems for 1,400 high-pressure dual-power unit cars (railway/transport LNG application).
market_consensus_gap: INOX India is seen as an industrial cryogenic tank maker. LNG mobility (railways/trucks) is an emerging, volume-scalable application that is not in estimates.
reflexivity_thesis: 1) Repeat LNG-mobility orders. 2) TAM expansion narrative. 3) Capital-goods fund interest. Risk: small order size.

news: NCC won a multi-village drinking water project worth Rs 1,076 cr.
market_consensus_gap: The market fears a JJM payment slowdown. New water awards suggest the funding pipeline is restarting.
reflexivity_thesis: 1) Inflow supports FY27 guidance. 2) A JJM funding revival narrative. Risk: routine order (low surprise).

catalyst_category: DGTR Sunset Review - ADD Continuation (Aluminium Foil)
news: DGTR recommended a 5-year extension of anti-dumping duty (USD 93.53-976.99/t) on aluminium foil (80 micron and below) from China, Thailand, Malaysia and Indonesia. Applicants: Hindalco, SRF Altech, Raviraj Foils, LSKB, Shree Venkateshwara Electrocast, Shyam Sel & Power. Awaiting the Finance Ministry.
market_consensus_gap: Continuation protects the downstream foil margins of domestic producers. It is a small part of Hindalco's consolidated EPS.
reflexivity_thesis: 1) Continuation of the duty keeps foil pricing stable. 2) Minor EPS support. Risk: low materiality.

catalyst_category: DGTR Sunset Review - ADD Continuation (Aluminium Foil)
news: SRF Altech (an SRF subsidiary) was a co-applicant in the aluminium foil ADD sunset review, where DGTR recommended a 5-year continuation.
market_consensus_gap: SRF's aluminium foil business is a newer diversification that is loss-making or low-return. Duty protection aids its ramp-up.
reflexivity_thesis: 1) Foil segment breakeven comes sooner. 2) Minor positive for the packaging segment. Risk: low materiality.
